key_concepts: Functions of circuit breakers, fuses, earthing, double insulation, and voltage regulators
Current increases as resistance decreases and becomes very large as resistance approaches
In a series circuit, one damaged bulb stops current in all other bulbs
In a parallel circuit, other bulbs still work if one bulb is damaged
Parallel circuits can overload when many appliances are used at the same time
Octopus connections plug several devices into one outlet and can cause overheating or over
Illegal connections using bare wires and no protective devices can cause fires and power i
Overloading can cause voltage drop and damage appliances
A short circuit may happen when worn-out wires expose their metallic part
A grounded circuit occurs when current returns through the metal casing of an appliance
Earthing directs excess current from an appliance casing to the ground
Double insulation prevents electric shock from grounded external casings
